texts.preamble: Anil Singh Sikarwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2020 Author: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari Bench: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari 1 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-49494-2019 (Anil Singh Sikarwar Vs. State of M.P.) Gwalior, Dated : 07/01/2020
texts.facts: The applicant has filed this second application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail. The first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 13/11/2019 passed in MCRC No.45492/2019. The applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.382/2019 registered at Police Station- Ambah, District- Morena for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 272, 273 and 120- B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Allegations against the applicant, in short, are that he along with co-accused Banwarilal Sharma was found involved in manufacturing food unsafe for human consumption at Milk Chiller Center of the co-accused, wherefrom two tankers containing 12000 litres of milk and a loading vehicle carrying 15 sacks of Exetrin powder were seized.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated. He is neither the owner of the Tankers nor of the business. The offences are triable by JMFC. Except section 420 of the IPC and 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, the rest are bailable in nature. There is no allegation of cheating against the applicant. Nothing has been seized from the applicant. There is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the evidence. With the aforesaid submissions, Anil Singh Sikarwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105060408/ 1 prayer for anticipatory bail is made. Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out. It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent/State that the investigation is pending and custodial interrogation may be required in the matter and the submission made by the counsel for the applicant has already been considered in previous bail application which was rejected by this Court.
